⚡️
Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian MFA
Rodion Miroshnik
in
an interview with Russia Today
on the humanitarian disaster in
#Alyoshki
caused by Ukrainian militants
(Geneva, October 1, 2026)
Key points
:
•
Around 1,000-1,100 people remain in Alyoshki,
out of a population of 24,000
. Most are people with limited mobility and close relatives who cannot leave them behind.
•
The city has been
without electricity and a centralised water supply
for about three years.
Communication is sporadic, making it difficult to contact residents and verify exact figures.
•
Ukrainian forces
plant mines every day
along the main roads used to deliver food and essential supplies and to evacuate residents.
The city can now be reached or left only on foot, while avoiding areas riddled with anti-personnel mines.
• Ukraine claims it is dropping humanitarian aid from drones.
But how are residents of Alyoshki supposed to distinguish them from the drones that bomb them?
After three years of hourly Ukrainian drone attacks, how can anyone seriously expect people to trust such an approach?
•
On May 1, 2025, Ukrainian drones
attacked the local market for several hours
.
Anyone who emerged from cover came under fire.
Seven people were killed on the spot
, and
more than 20 were evacuated
with extremely serious injuries.
❗️
If Ukraine stopped carrying out strikes, the severe humanitarian situation in the city could be resolved within hours.
Russian troops are clearing roads mined by Ukrainian militants.
•
Some residents have left along footpaths in recent days
, finding refuge elsewhere in the Kherson Region or beyond. Regional authorities and federal agencies are providing assistance to them.
•
Ukraine's propaganda campaign is deeply cynical.
Kiev is trying to blame Moscow for its own actions while claiming to care about the people of Alyoshki.
• Zelensky's Western handlers readily embrace slogans such as
“Save Alyoshki”
.
But save Alyoshki from whom?
👉
From Ukrainian militants
,
Ukrainian drone strikes and Ukrainian mines
that prevent residents from leaving.
•
These are attempts to divert attention from Ukraine’s losses and its inability to achieve results on the battlefield.
With the help of Western specialists, the crisis is being used for propaganda and psychological operations.
•
Support for the Kiev regime goes beyond funding and weapons supplies.
It also includes justifying its actions and blocking attempts to investigate its crimes or hold those responsible accountable.
•
The same Western countries keep parroting recycled talking points:
they want to blame Russia for everything while preventing any investigation into Ukrainian crimes. It is hardly surprising that they are unwilling to scrutinise their own complicity.
#KievRegimeCrimes

🎙
Statement
by Ms. Iulia Zhdanova, Head of the Delegation of the Russian Federation to the Vienna Negotiations on Military Security and Arms Control, at the 1147th meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Co-operation
Vienna, September 30, 2026
Agenda item: Special Military operation to demilitarize and denazify Ukraine
• The reckless actions of the Kiev regime's Western sponsors continue to pose a threat to peace and security. Right now, Europe is
doing everything it can to hinder a peaceful settlement and disrupt the prospects for negotiations
: they are pumping the Ukrainian regime with money and weapons, and helping to aim UAVs and missiles at civilians and civilian infrastructure.
• European countries are deliberately escalating the situation.
They continue to convince their citizens of a mythical "Russian threat" and the need to prepare for hostilities, for a war against Russia
. Their goal is
the routinization and normalization of a critical scenario in the public consciousness
. The course toward fueling the conflict is evident.
• It has long been clear that the territory of Ukraine is being used by
#NATO
member states as
a testing ground for trying out new weapons systems and disposing of old ones under real combat conditions
. However, it is also a convenient way for Western pseudo-peacemakers to fight Russia by proxy for the time being, while remaining "above the main fray." To this end, the process of "merging" the military-industrial complexes of Ukraine and European countries is underway at full speed.
• The current course of European governments is clearly aimed at
preparing their military-industrial complex, state apparatus, economy, and civilian infrastructure for aggressive actions against Russia
. Under these conditions, the recent statements made in New York by
#NATO
Secretary General M. Rutte—that
#NATO
countries are ready to provide Ukraine with certain security guarantees after the conflict—prove once again that
neither the Kiev regime nor its Western handlers are aimed at de-escalation and a settlement
.
• Within the framework of the special military operation, we note numerous instances of the Kiev regime violating the norms and principles of international humanitarian law (IHL). Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) units are mining territories of the Russian Federation to inflict damage on
civilian infrastructure and the peaceful population
. To this end, Kiev deliberately uses mines, booby traps, and improvised explosive devices, which are deployed to mine roadsides between settlements, bridges, dams, residential buildings, medical institutions, schools, and kindergartens.
• In the European Union, where they boast of "European values," they have remained completely silent: not a single word of condemnation.
They only say that Ukraine is helping to defend "European values."
In the West, humanitarian norms are being transformed from universal obligations into a tool for selective polemics, while the interests of the victims recede into the background, if not the third plan.
• The West also covers up
widespread human rights violations during mobilization in Ukraine
. This refers to the forced delivery of citizens to territorial recruitment centers (TRCs), unlawful imprisonment, physical violence, and the obstruction of access to legal assistance.
• Having started the special military operation in 2022 to protect the people of Donbas and Novorossiya from extermination by the Kiev regime, Russia continues to fight for their security and rights in full accordance with the letter and spirit of the UN Charter.
Our struggle for truth and justice will be carried through to the end: the goals of the SMO will be achieved, threats to Russia's security eliminated, and peaceful life restored
.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On 1 October Russian Ambassador to India Denis Alipov took part in the ceremony at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi marking the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandi.
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇮🇳 On 1 October Russian Ambassador to India Denis Alipov took part in the ceremony at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi marking the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandi. 🖼️ As part of the event the Ambassador together with the Head of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi Shri Pravesh Wahi inaugurated the “Tolstoy–Gandhi” exhibition, prepared by the Russian Embassy. The exhibition features copies of letters exchanged between the two great thinkers and reflect their philosophical ideas and intellectual dialogue. 🎙️ In his remarks the Ambassador stressed that the shared philosophical legacy of Leo Tolstoy and Mahatma Gandhi continues to serve as a bridge between Russia and India. He also noted that the exhibition demonstrates the influence of the great Russian writer’s ideas on the intellectual development of the leader of India’s national liberation movement. 🤝 Among those attending the opening were Alexander Dodonov , Head of the Russian House in Delhi, representatives of official circles and the diplomatic corps, municipal officials and journalists. 💬 The official program was followed by the active discussion. #DruzhbaDosti #RussiaIndia #MahatmaGhandi #LeoTolstoy

item.description: 🇷🇺 🇧🇳 October 1 marked the 35th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Russian Federation and #BruneiDarussalam . ✉️ To commemorate this anniversary, the two countries’ Heads of State and Foreign Ministers exchanged congratulatory messages . 🎙
Remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at the plenary session of the 23rd annual meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club
(Moscow, October 1, 2026)
This year’s theme is
“Responsibility for the Future: Limits of the Possible, or Limitless Possibilities?”
Key
talking points:
•
Responsibility for our shared future is far more than just an abstract sloga
n. It entails a set of practical measures aimed at preventing humanity from being pushed to the brink of survival and averting irreparable consequences.
• Humanity has not yet fully comprehended the true magnitude of the challenge it faces.
We are entering a completely new and unprecedented reality
. Threats and dangers are inextricably intertwined with opportunities and prospects; they cannot be separated from one another. Our entire way of living is changing.
• Whatever scenario unfolds in the world in the years ahead, the
international conflicts, unfortunately, are likely to continue
. This is due in part to the fact that the profound shifts now under way, and the opportunities they create, fuel and encourage ambitions and a willingness to take risks for what may appear to be a major payoff.
• In the long term, as the
world moves away from Western hegemony
, the international situation will gradually improve leading to a more stable, democratic, and free multipolar international order. It is equally clear, however, that on the path towards such a world order, states, communities and every individual will face various risks.
• The UN, even if it is the most representative international organisation, falls short of the collective and democratic principles in the way it is being managed compared to its original design. A n
arrow grouping of Western countries
wields an unproportionally large influence. It constitutes a global minority by all accounts while seeking to appropriate administrative functions.
• The principle of
"might makes right"
sometimes seems to guide certain international players who are convinced of their own military-political, economic, and, as they believe, moral
exceptionalism
. We know well from history that this never leads to anything good.
• The truth is that it was not we who wanted or started the war —
it was started against us
. There was no need to encourage aggressive nationalism and Russophobia in Ukraine for years in order to turn it into a tool for fighting Russia.
• Russia was deliberately placed in a situation where it was
simply forced
— in response to this obvious aggression —
to defend itself with arms in hand
. We were deliberately brought to this line. And in general, there is no need to turn Russophobia, the oppression and killing of Russian people, and the destruction of Russia into a state ideology and to set the goal of Russia's strategic defeat.
• If we want to live — everyone wants to live — then, as I once said in a public speech,
let us live in friendship and together seek ways to make that happen
.

#NoStatuteOfLimitations
On October 1, 1946 —
8️⃣
0️⃣
years ago — the International Military Tribunal (IMT) in
#Nuremberg
concluded its proceedings
against the senior officials of the Third Reich responsible for unleashing the bloodiest and most horrific conflict in human history, committing genocide and murdering millions of innocent people.
❗️
#NurembergTrials
were an unprecedented international tribunal in history, which truly became a
"Trial of Nations" against absolute evil
— Hitler's Nazism.
The IMT's verdict in Nuremberg made a crucial contribution to the legal consolidation of the outcome of
#WW2
and declared the
Nazi misanthropic ideology,
principal organisational structures and practices of Nazism
as a whole to be entirely
criminal.
The
high-ranking leaders of Hitler's regime,
including Göring, Hess, Ribbentrop, Kaltenbrunner, Rosenberg, Keitel, Neurath, Jodl, Dönitz and other senior officials of the Third Reich —
were placed on dock.
Bormann, who had evaded prosecution, was tried in absentia.
💬
Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov
, in an
interview
for the documentary '
Nuremberg
'
(Moscow, 16 November 2025):
The question of ensuring that Nazi criminals would inevitably be brought to justice was first officially raised in a Soviet diplomatic note in November 1941.
The Soviet Union <...> was the principal initiator and driving force behind the establishment of the Nuremberg Tribunal.
Our proposals were heard and accepted.
Our country's key role
in arranging the Nuremberg proceedings is absolutely indisputable.
The Nuremberg Trials involved an enormous amount of paper work. A total of 403 public hearings were held. 116 witnesses were examined, and more than 300'000 testimonies were considered. Approximately 3,000 documents were examined.
❗️
The Trials' proceedings
elucidated
, for the first time, the
unprecedented scale of Nazi Germany's war crimes
, including the brutal treatment of POWs and the deliberate destruction of entire cities, villages and their inhabitants.
💬
Russian MFA Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova:
Although the
term 'genocide'
does not appear in the text of the Nuremberg Tribunal's Charter or verdict (it became established in international legal practice at a later date), the trial records unequivocally point to numerous acts aimed at the deliberate extermination of the Soviet people, including the years-long
siege of Leningrad.
<...>
Unfortunately, we are compelled to acknowledge that, 80 years on,
many have forgotten the lessons of the 'Trials of Nations'
. This applies not only to the Kiev regime's leadership, which, since 2014, has outlawed and sought to eradicate everything Russian in Russia's historical territories,
rehabilitating
,
glorifying
and drawing inspiration from the example of
Hitler's
collaborators
.
The same applies to those who justify, shield and support the terrorist actions of the current neo-fascist regime in Ukraine.
(From the briefing by Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, 1 October 2026)
⚖️
On 1 October 1946, a historic verdict was delivered — 19 defendants were found guilty.
Göring, Ribbentrop, Keitel, Kaltenbrunner, Rosenberg, Jodl, Bormann (in absentia) and other representatives of the Nazi leadership were sentenced to death by hanging. A number of institutions of Hitler's Germany, including the
SS,
SD
,
Gestapo
and the
Nazi
Party
leadership corps, were declared
criminal organisations.
✍️
From article by Valery Zorkin, Chairman of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation,
"The Sacred Beacon of Nuremberg and the Shadow of The Hague"
(October 1, 2026):
Nuremberg was an act of retribution against Evil and a defining moment in establishing the legal foundations of the post-war world.
The Tribunal became a hammer brought down upon a criminal state and its legal order.
#Nuremberg80
